parts.note: 2 down is a cricketer's score of nothing, so the clue asks for the moment of nought, a phrase for the critical start time of an operation

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a DUCK (2 down) is a batsman's score of zero, which is the pun behind the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the scheduled moment an operation or attack begins, punningly the hour of a nought.

clue.text: A failure at 15 to take evasive action

definitions.meaning: in cricket (15 across) a batsman out for no runs has made a nought, the classic failure
to dip the head quickly to dodge something

explanation.surface: Someone flops at a sport and tries to dodge the consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer out without scoring has made this nought; as a verb it means to bob down out of harm's way.

clue.text: Rope was tangled inside that lady

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit inside the pronoun, so this word signals the container

parts.note: that lady is referred to as her

indicators.note: tangled means the letters of the word beside it are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A rope got tangled around some woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rope' at the start is the definition; 'tangled' acts on the short word 'was', and 'inside' puts the result within the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or cable used for mooring or towing ships.

clue.text: 2 away from 6 14s and a raised level

indicators.note: away from tells us one piece is taken out of the six-ball set that follows

parts.note: six deliveries (14 across) make a cricket over
2 down, a nought or duck, looks like the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cross-reference puzzle line about removing items from a set and adding a raised platform.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER in cricket is six balls bowled; a duck (2 down) is zero, shown as O, so 'away from' leaves VER.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed platform raised along the outside of a house, a raised level of floor.

indicators.note: out loud signals that the phrase is to be said rather than spelt

parts.note: a peeler is an old British slang word for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel

explanation.surface: A bowler appeals to a passing constable by shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: PEELER is old British slang for a police officer, from Robert Peel who founded the Metropolitan Police; A PEELER sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler (12 across) asking the umpire 'howzat?' for a wicket is making an appeal, hence one who appeals.

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in a bad state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy, impoverished nation is miserable from end to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' signals an anagram of SAD ALL OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: El Salvador is a small Central American country.

definitions.meaning: a cricketer (15 across with -er) who bats first in the innings
the second part of 13 down is a key, and a key is a device that opens a lock

explanation.definitionFit: An opening batsman starts the innings; a key is something that opens, so both are things that start or unlock.

indicators.note: having lost tells us a piece is dropped from the gambling word

parts.note: to speculate is to gamble or bet
7 down is an opener, here the first letter of the word being cut

explanation.surface: A man called Nick has placed a wager but lost a game opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is OPENER, so the 'opener' of SPECULATE, its first letter S, is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To peculate is to embezzle, so it means to nick or steal in British slang.

clue.text: Place of learning once first to propagate growth

parts.note: a poly, short for polytechnic, was a type of British college before 1992 when they became universities

indicators.note: first to picks out the initial letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An old college pioneered a way to cultivate plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small abnormal growth of tissue, as in the nose or bowel.

definitions.meaning: a cricket shot played across the line to a short ball

explanation.surface: A fielder takes a catch off a cricket stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook catches fish or holds coats; in cricket it is also a pulled shot off a bouncer.

clue.text: 15er — he needs an answer when spinning

indicators.note: spinning tells us the letters whirl round into a new order, apt for a spin bowler

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer needs a response when bowling spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when spinning' shuffles HE plus AN ANSWER; 'needs' just joins them. Shane Warne was a great Australian leg-spin bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Shane Warne was a famous Australian Test cricketer, the leg-spinner.

definitions.meaning: a cricketer who delivers the ball; the 's stands for is
a hard round felt hat, the derby

explanation.surface: A cricketer's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler delivers the ball in cricket, and a bowler is also a hard round felt hat.

parts.note: Tony Lock and Rob Key were England cricketers; joined by and, their names form the phrase for something kept safely locked up

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means safely locked away, as in kept secure under it.

parts.note: a birth is the bringing of a baby into the world; in cricket the word for one ball bowled is the same

explanation.definitionFit: Giving birth is the delivery of a baby, and a ball bowled in cricket is likewise called this.

parts.note: a century is a hundred runs, so the sport where centuries are scored

explanation.definitionFit: A century of a hundred runs by one batsman is the landmark score in this bat-and-ball sport.

clue.text: Secured during climbing of steeple, journeys alone?

indicators.note: during places one piece within the other, the obtained word in the middle
climbing in a down clue makes the word read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a steeple is a spire
secured means got, as in obtained

explanation.surface: Someone climbs a church steeple and goes on solitary trips.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' means read upward, so backwards; 'during' places the obtained word within. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego trips are acts of self-indulgence, jokingly trips taken by the ego on its own.

indicators.note: collecting means the villain takes in a letter, so it is the container

parts.note: the devil is a bad man
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A diabolical cricketer piles up runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Bradman was the great Australian batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Donald Bradman was Australia's legendary Test batsman.

clue.text: US girl, amid mild expletive, dismissing 7

indicators.note: amid puts the girl's name in the middle of the trimmed oath
dismissing means a letter is sent away from the oath

parts.note: damn is a mild swear word
7 down is an opener, here the first letter of the oath
Erica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An American girl swears mildly as a batsman is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'opener' (7 down) of DAMN, D, is dismissed, leaving AMN; ERICA goes amid it.
explanation.definitionFit: US is used as an adjective for things from the United States, the same as American.

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the string of compass points

parts.note: compass points are quarters: E, S, S, E, N, E
C is the standard abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Wild nature is chilly all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: The four quarters of the compass give letters E, S, N, W; 'many' of them here run ESSENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is the intrinsic nature or core character of something.

clue.text: Figures so reversible carrying label in blue

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed little word holds the rest within it
reversible tells us the word next to it is turned round
in puts the tag inside the political colour

parts.note: blue is the Conservative colour, so a Tory, CON
a label is a tag

explanation.surface: Some reversible garment shapes carry a label in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversible' turns SO into OS; TAG goes 'in' CON (blue, the Conservative Party colour), and OS is 'carrying' CTAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: Octagons are geometric figures with eight sides.

clue.text: Might 15er leave his to stop maintaining resistance?

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the word for stop holds the letter inside

parts.note: to cease is to stop
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Would a cricketer leave his post to stop holding out?
explanation.walkthrough: A batsman who steps out of his crease, the line marking his ground, can be stumped or run out.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is the white line a batsman stands behind; leaving it risks being stumped.

parts.note: the House of York was an English royal dynasty
a Windsor queen, Elizabeth Regina, is ER

explanation.surface: A ball bowled by the royal house of Windsor.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth II of the House of Windsor. A YORKER is a delivery (14) pitched at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A yorker is a cricket delivery aimed to land at the batsman's feet.

clue.text: With this, salute the old ship, one close to harbour

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
SS stands for steamship
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: close to picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Greeting the old ship as it nears the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Saluting an officer, one says this respectful reply of obedience.

parts.note: something sore is tender
a ness is a headland, a head of land

explanation.surface: A sore head brings sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbouring capes or Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is gentleness and compassion towards others.

parts.note: a cricketing blunder; the word for a small error is also a close fielding position

explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, and also a fielding position beside the wicketkeeper in cricket.

clue.text: If 12s hit this, one's stitched up!

definitions.text: If 12s hit this, one's stitched up!

parts.words: If 12s hit this, one's stitched up!
parts.note: bowlers aim for the raised stitching on the ball; stitched up also means framed or done for

explanation.definitionFit: The seam is the stitched ridge on a cricket ball, which bowlers try to land on.

clue.text: 15 shot, one clearing the way for Father Christmas?

definitions.meaning: a cricket shot played on one knee

definitions.text: one clearing the way for Father Christmas?
definitions.meaning: a chimney cleaner, who clears the route Santa takes

explanation.surface: A cricket stroke and a chimney cleaner who helps Santa.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweep is a cricket stroke; a chimney sweep cleans the flue down which Santa supposedly comes.

definitions.meaning: a left-arm wrist-spin delivery in cricket
a porcelain figure, which would be labelled breakable

explanation.surface: A ball bowled, and an ornament labelled as breakable.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old cricket term for a left-armer's wrist-spun ball, and literally a man made of porcelain.
